html:
Barkcloth in Uganda is made by the Baganda from the inner bark of the mutuba fig tree, which is stripped, soaked and beaten with wooden mallets into a soft reddish brown cloth.

For centuries it was worn by kings, chiefs and ordinary people, used for burial shrouds and offered at ceremonies. Craftsmen of a special clan made barkcloth for the royal court of Buganda.

Cotton cloth brought by traders and missionaries pushed it aside in daily wear, but it remained central at funerals, coronations and cultural events. UNESCO listed barkcloth making in Uganda in 2005 as an intangible heritage, alongside the royal shrines of the Kasubi Tombs.
sum: Barkcloth in Uganda is made by the Baganda from the inner bark of the mutuba fig tree, which is stripped, soaked and beaten with wooden mallets into a soft reddish brown cloth.
